messages:
alex_cs: Heads up — ACME reported a month-end mismatch. Dashboard shows 1,142,301 tokens for Feb but invoice line item is 1,057,200 tokens. Totals don't line up: dashboard $12,345 vs invoice $11,431. They also say the dashboard shows 'Pro' for Feb but invoice applied 'Starter' proration on 2026-02-28. Invoice ID INV-2026-02-ACME. Can someone triage? :eyes:

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-02-ACME generated: https://billing.redwood.example/invoices/INV-2026-02-ACME :page_with_curl: (auto-notice)

maria_billing: thx Alex. Can you paste org_id + subscription_id? Also: did they change plan mid-month or use multiple API keys/regions? Often parser windows/timezone cause this.

alex_cs: org_id: org_0xACME, subscription_id: sub_0xACME_FEB26. They switched plan at 2026-02-28T23:50:00Z (migrated to Pro). Region: us-west-2. No multiple keys afaik.

sam_eng: quick checklist: 1) meter-processor dedupe window 2) aggregation window alignment (UTC midnight vs tenant timezone) 3) duplicate streaming token events when connection resets. Can you export the raw usage CSV from console and attach? Also helpful: a sample request_id from Feb 28 they flagged.

jess_support: I asked ACME for a screenshot and a sample request-id. They sent one: r-ff4a9b2c. Said the dashboard shows 1.14M tokens on the usage page export.

maria_billing: I'm checking invoice line items. I see a proration entry on 2026-03-01 00:00 with plan_id starter_2025 -> pro_2026 and an invoice-level credit of -$914. That credit might explain part of the difference but not tokens. Invoice token count is lower than dashboard by ~85k tokens. Could be double counting on dashboard or late-processing credits on invoice.

sam_eng: paste this SQL run in metering DB to compare raw events vs aggregated totals:

```
SELECT date_trunc('day', event_ts) as day, sum(tokens) as raw_tokens, sum(aggregated_tokens) as agg_tokens
FROM metering.raw_events
WHERE org_id = 'org_0xACME' AND event_ts >= '2026-02-01' AND event_ts < '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
```

sam_eng: also check meter-processor logs for run-20260301-01 (the nightly job that finalizes aggregates). Use: `kubectl logs -n billing meter-processor-20260301 -c processor | grep org_0xACME`

maria_billing: running the queries now. FYI the invoice generator reads from aggregates table (metering.aggregates_final) at 2026-03-01T00:05Z. Dashboard reads from live window that includes streaming deltas. If the streaming pipeline duplicated events, dashboard could be higher.

alex_cs: customer insists they didn't do any unusual traffic; they're worried about being charged wrong tier. Can we confirm which plan ID the invoice actually applied?

maria_billing: invoice records: applied_plan_id = starter_2025 for period start 2026-02-01, then proration applied at 2026-02-28 23:50 for pro_2026 effective 2026-03-01. That matches their note — invoice billed Starter for Feb and prorated toward Pro for March. The dashboard shows 'Pro' because subscription was toggled in the console before midnight and dashboard reflects the latest state. There's a mismatch in timing semantics.

sam_eng: I found suspicious log entries: meter-processor had a recent release that changed dedupe window from 2m -> 2s (typo in env var). That would let near-duplicate streaming events slip through into live aggregates, inflating dashboard counts, while nightly job deduped correctly for invoice aggregates.

maria_billing: aha. That would explain why dashboard > invoice. The invoice system uses the finalized aggregates (post-dedup) and also applies credits/adjustments. Dashboard reads the near-real-time stream that relied on the short dedupe window.

jess_support: Can we confirm magnitude? How many extra tokens were counted?

sam_eng: running ad-hoc dedupe check now. Preliminary: ~88,743 tokens duplicated across several streaming sessions on Feb 27-28 for org_0xACME (connection resets + retransmit).

maria_billing: that matches the ~85k gap. Good. Root cause looks like misconfigured dedupe window after recent deploy (PR #789).

sam_eng: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/789 (config typo). Fix merged in 789-fix-dedupe. Deployed rollback and added integration test.

maria_billing: remediation plan: 1) run backfill to recompute realtime aggregates for Feb for affected orgs (job backfill-20260301-org_0xACME). 2) Recompute invoice adjustments and issue credit if necessary. 3) Publish incident note and notify ACME. I've queued a backfill and will run it after approvals.

alex_cs: Draft reply to ACME: "Thanks for flagging — we found a deduplication config bug that inflated dashboard tokens late Feb. Our invoice generator used the corrected aggregates so the invoice was lower; we'll backfill and, if that increases invoice charges, we'll issue a corresponding adjustment or provide a credit to make it right. We'll keep you updated." Thoughts? :slightly_smiling_face:

jess_support: sounds good. Offer them a one-time courtesy credit for the confusion (small token credit) and fast-track any billing questions. Also flag for escalation if they push.

maria_billing: applied temporary credit hold for ACME while we complete backfill. I'll confirm when backfill + any billing adjustments are done. Tentative ETA 6 hours.

sam_eng: backfill run started: job backfill-20260301-org_0xACME (watching logs). Command: `kubectl exec -n billing job/backfill-20260301 -- /bin/backfill --org org_0xACME --period 2026-02-01/2026-03-01`

maria_billing: backfill finished. Adjusted aggregated tokens for Feb: dashboard corrected to 1,057,210 (matches invoice within rounding). Applied credit: $0 (no charge change) — because invoice already used finalized aggregates; we sent ACME a clarifying note and offered a $100 courtesy credit for disruption.

alex_cs: sending customer note now, offering $100 credit + explanation. Marking as resolved on our side.

jess_support: filing incident and short postmortem: incident/metering-20260301-dedupe. I'll assign owners and post link here when available.

sam_eng: added commit + CI fix: sha1 abcdef123456, merged PR 789-fix-dedupe. Also added an integration test for streaming dedupe timing.

maria_billing: closing the loop: invoice totals are correct; dashboard transiently showed inflated tokens due to streaming dedupe config. We reconciled counts and issued a goodwill $100 credit. ACME confirmed acceptance. :white_check_mark:

alex_cs: thanks everyone — good catch. :party_parrot:
